items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1959-06-30
items.q: So I got a letter from my uncle Paul and I told him what had happened. He said, I'll send you a banjo. He went back to Chicago. He was with King Oliver. So, he sent me a little small banjo.

ctx.x: Who did Lloyd Arthur Dog play with?

He played with the Arnold Brass Band. They played first clarinet. He died young with a social disease. My great-aunt term. He was a shy boy. He was a basketball sergeant. Some sportswoman enticed him and got in a corral and contacted his disease. And they wouldn't tell the old folks that he was sick. And somehow they detected that he had this trouble. And when they found out about it and rushed him to the hospital, it was too late. So he died of this sickness. And this is just a lot on the planet. So Michael Paul…
Back to Florida for a minute. What were the bands like in Florida other than the band you were with?

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He had me going. He owned one. He had a clarinet. He let me blow it. Showed me how to blow it

ctx.x: Who was considered the best trumpet player in New Orleans?

It was Buddy Petit. I’ll tell you that. I never heard Bunk at his heights, but I don’t think Bunk . . . My uncle Paul said Bunk was the greatest, but I think maybe Bud had taken some of the . . . younger than Bunk. Maybe he had something he snatched from Bunk, because Bunk disappeared around 1918, 1919.
Yeah, I think it was the teens.

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: They showed me how to hold the sticks properly... So he let me blow the clarinet... So he sent me to Barney Bigard.

ctx.x: The changes. And three chords, C-F-G. But in the meantime, I had been around my uncle Paul between his visits from Chicago, and my uncle Louis and them, and they all got this drum set up, and they'd play... All of them played the drums. So I could get by on the drums, too. They showed me how to hold the sticks properly and they let me play. And my aunt had bought a victrola, and they'd go borrow the victrola in (?), and they'd play against the victrola. And they'd let me play. Then I thought about all them drums…

So my Uncle Paul has got a clarinet. He's foolin' around with the clarinet. Can't play it. He's foolin' around, but he's learning to... I found out later that he was learning so he could count, count notation to write, because he wanted to write. So he figured he'd play a little melody and he'd be able to. So he let me blow the clarinet. A lift-off(?) point. He told me, 'Go take some lessons.'
